title: Elastic Staircase Shedding orchestrator and regional escalation policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a new load-shedding orchestrator called 'Elastic Staircase Shedding' (ESS). ESS introduces stepped priority bands that can grow and shrink (the "staircase") based on observed token pressure and SLO health, combined with a regional escalation policy that coordinates circuit breakers and cross-region failover. The ticket covers design, prototype, infra changes to admission controller, rollout, and dashboards.
background: Current shedding approaches use fixed priority lanes and per-tenant token buckets which either underutilize capacity during mild spikes or fail to degrade gracefully during sustained overload. Operators frequently have to tune static thresholds per-region. We need an adaptive, telemetry-driven mechanism that: 1) preserves high-priority real-time requests, 2) provides predictable SLO mappings for customers, and 3) coordinates safe multi-region failover and circuit breaker escalation without causing cascading retries.
proposal_summary:
1) Introduce Elastic Staircase: instead of fixed discrete queues, define N stair steps each with a dynamic width in concurrent requests/tokens that expands or contracts based on short-window occupancy and SLO burn rate.
2) Tokenized admission hints: callers can attach a token hint (0-100) representing request criticality; ESS maps hints to stair steps and enforces fractional admission probabilities during pressure.
3) Regional circuit-breaker tiers: per-region CB state machine (OK -> Throttling -> HardOpen) with escalation windows that coordinate with adjacent regions via meta-health heartbeats.
4) Graceful degradation modes: partial responses, compressed payloads, model-variant fallbacks (smaller model), and preconfigured 'cheap-path' transforms.
5) Operator controls and safety: emergency hard-stop, shadow-shedding simulation mode, and rollbackable rollout via console feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: ESS prototype exposes stair step occupancy and admission decisions in traces and metrics.
Under a synthetic spike test, P99 latency for P0 requests must remain within SLO target (<= 250ms) while overall throughput drops gracefully.
Circuit breaker escalation prevents more than one region from entering HardOpen simultaneously for the same tenant (unless global outage).
Rollback path: toggling feature flag returns system to current fixed-priority behavior with no request loss.
Automated chaos tests show that ESS does not increase retry storms: retry amplification ratio <= 1.2 compared to baseline.
Docs and runbook updated with operator playbook and dashboard links.
implementation_notes: Admission controller changes: add stair-step allocator component; admission decisions must be idempotent and cacheable for short TTLs.
Telemetry: new metrics ess.step_occupancy{region,step}, ess.admit_rate{region,step,tenant_tier}, ess.slo_burn_rate{tenant}.
Circuit breaker: implement tiered timers (min_hold, probation) and cross-region heartbeat aggregation with 500ms max staleness.
Graceful modes: integrate with response pipeline to support 'partial-output' header and structured 'degradation_reason' JSON field for downstream clients.
Backwards compatible: default behavior when no token hint provided maps to tenant's configured priority band.
Persisted config: use existing config service with new ESS policy schema; include per-tenant caps and emergency overrides.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature gated deploy of ESS in shadow mode in us-west-2 for 5% of traffic. Collect metrics and validate admission decisions match safe thresholds.
Week 2: Canary: enable SHEding for internal tenants in us-west-2 under moderate traffic; run chaos tests (load, GC spikes).
Week 3: Incremental enable for external low-risk tenants and enable cross-region heartbeat aggregation in read-only mode (no failover).
Week 4: Full enable in a single region, with auto-escalation disabled (manual control). Validate dashboards and runbook steps.
Week 5: Gradual multi-region enable with circuit-breaker escalation active; monitor SLOs and retry amplification. If >2% customer-impacting errors, rollback to previous config.
Emergency rollback: global feature flag off -> revert to legacy admission controller.
metrics: ess.step_occupancy{region,step}: occupancy percentage of each stair step
ess.admit_rate{region,step,tenant_tier}: accepted requests per second by step
ess.slo_burn_rate{tenant}: SLO burn rate computed over 5m/1h windows
cb.state_changes{region,tenant}: transitions and durations for circuit breakers
retry_amplification_ratio: ratio of retries induced by ESS admission decisions vs baseline
p99_latency_p0{region}: latency tail for P0 requests
test_plan: Unit tests for stair allocator logic and admission probability math.
Integration tests simulating tenant mixes (PLG + enterprise) under bursty traffic patterns.
Chaos: network partition between regions while ESS is active to validate non-cascading failover.
Load: synthetic token storms to verify graceful degradation modes trigger and partial responses include expected metadata.
A/B: compare customer-facing error rates and p99 latency with control fleet over a 48-hour window.
notes: 2025-09-29: Kickoff with runtime, infra, and SRE. Initial staircase sizing heuristics proposed (exponential step widths).
2025-10-02: Telemetry schema reviewed; added ess.slo_burn_rate to trigger automated contraction of staircase.
2025-10-04: Prototype admission simulator completed; observed retry amplification 1.05 in synthetic tests.
